newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: GUIDE - CZECH LOWER HOUSE FEBRUARY SESSION.
newsitem.headline: GUIDE - CZECH LOWER HOUSE FEBRUARY SESSION.

text.p: The lower house of the Czech parliament continues its February session on Wednesday, after it approved an extensive 88-point agenda when the chamber convened on February 4.
The session is expected to continue through much of the month.
The major point to be debated on Wednesday is the Czech-German post-World War Two reconciliation declaration which has already been signed by both countries' governments.
Deputies voted to begin debate on the issue on Tuesday.

Major points scheduled for debate on the draft agenda for the rest of the session include the realignment of the common border with Slovakia, already agreed by both governments, and the report on the special commission investigating the failure of Kreditni Banka a.s..
The house usually follows the agenda in order, after the conclusion of the previous item.
Below is a summary of key agenda items in the February session and their place on the agenda: - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
SECOND READINGS 5. Measures on relations with Libya 6. Law on property assessment 8. Constitutional ammendment to change
common border with Slovakia 10. Government draft on social subsidies to balance an
increase in heating prices 12. Changes to the law on General Health Insurance (VZP)
FIRST READING 26. Government draft law on anti-dumping protection
THIRD READINGS 43. Measures on relations with Libya 44. Law on property assessment 46. Constitutional ammendment to change
common border with Slovakia 47. Government draft on social subsidies to balance an
increase in heating prices 52. Changes to the law on General Health Insurance (VZP)
ONLY ONE READING REQUIRED 56. Czech-German Declaration on mutual relations
REPORTS TO PARLIAMENT 57. Government report on crisis situation in state railways 70. Report on situation at steel factory Poldi Kladno 75. Report of the chairman of the special parliamentary
commission investigating the failure of Kreditni Banka
a.s..

Note. Standard laws must receive final approval in the lower house by a simple majority of those present voting for the measure in its third reading. Constitutional laws or ammendments require a three-fifths majority voting for the measure in its third reading.

The upper house, the Senate, must consider all measures passed by the lower house -- except for the state budget which requires no Senate approval -- within 30 days. If a measure is approved by the lower house and not considered by the Senate within 30 days, it automatically goes to the president for final consideration.

Any rejection of a lower-house approved measure by the president or the Senate, returns to the lower house, but can be approved again using the same voting rules on the original consideration of the measure in the lower house, at which point the measure must become law.
-- Prague Newsroom, 42-2-2423-0003
